lens: Capacity code: AS/NZS 4600:2018 and AISI S100-16 forms in analysis/liftcalc/as4600.py, the member, joint and link checks in liftcase.py, and the added-part checks in connectors.py / run_connectors.py
summary:
I found no errors in the capacity formulas themselves. My hand checks match the code to 3 significant figures: compression at L = 600 mm gives 29.23 kN, the minor-axis moment 0.363 kNm, one 10 gauge screw 1.77 kN, M12 bolt bearing 10.13 kN on the 1.5 mm strap and 5.21 kN on 0.95 mm at 412.5 MPa. The axis and buckling-length mapping in check_members is also right. My run of the 11 design cases reproduced the log (max member 0.910, max joint 0.834).

The pass result, however, depends on five things the capacity code does not check or the design basis does not state:
(1) An undocumented 1200 mm cap on the twisting length (liftcase.py:99). If the twisting length equals the stated out-of-plane length, 4 members fail at 1.19 to 1.61. Lateral buckling in minor-axis bending is also not coded.
(2) The cradle and foot-plate screw check pools 3 stations together. The repo's own forces put 1.06 to 1.45 on the 4 screws at the plate-end stations of 6 plates.
(3) Six south-wall stud bases pass only with bearing credit. Without it they are at 1.04 to 1.82. No stud end-gap limit is stated and there is no web crippling check.
(4) Screw end distance is not checked. Framer puts the wall diagonal-brace end screws 2.8 to 4.2 mm from the member end (code minimum 1.5d = 7.3 mm). The coded but unused AS/NZS-style form gives 1.43 there.
(5) Framer operations are ignored: lip notches at every chord web joint, swaged web ends, and service holes, including in the two most loaded studs.

Minor items: member shear and combined bending + shear are unchecked (0.35 and 0.43 by my check); the basis for the 0.363 kNm minor-axis value needs stating, and the lips-in-compression distortional check is missing; strength values for the G450 parts are not consistent with the research basis; bolt tear-out and lifting-head pin-bearing logic; 10.5 % vs 5 % sideways allowance; the cited test_as4600.py does not exist.

No repo file was modified. Scratch scripts and outputs are in <home>/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/e779ede6ae5bcc20/240dc1af-6f85-4fbd-ae6d-ded96ca243c4/scratchpad/review_capacity/ (caps.py, caps2.py, minor_ltb.py, post.py + post_out.txt, plate_nodes.py + plate_nodes_out.txt, bearing_off.py + bearing_off_out.txt, end_dist.py + end_dist_out.txt, foot_2mm.py + foot_2mm_out.txt). Note: commit 0ffaff8 changed only labels in run_lift.py during the review; no effect on the results.

findings.title: Twisting length is an undocumented 1200 mm cap, and the zero-failures result depends on it
findings.detail: member_lengths returns L_tw = max(L_in, min(L_out, 1200)). DESIGN_BASIS §5 defines only the in-plane and out-of-plane lengths. The 1200 mm matches no restraint position: roof truss chords have no bridging over 3122 mm, and studs are 2659 mm between out-of-plane holds. Flexural-torsional buckling uses fox(L_out) with foz(L_tw), so this number sets phiNc for every long compression member. I re-checked the 11 design cases with L_tw = L_out (the stated out-of-plane basis) and 4 members go over 1.0: end roof truss top chords NFT46 1.61 and NFT26 1.57 (phiNc 4.56 kN vs N = 6.8 kN), floor truss top chord NFT4 1.20 (phiNc 12.71 vs N = 13.2 kN), stud W7 1.19. With L_tw = L_in the maximum is 0.68. Lateral buckling in minor-axis bending with the lips in compression (AS/NZS 4600 3.3.3.2.1(b) / AISI F2.1.2, j = 49.8 mm) is not coded. It is harmless at L_tw <= 1200 (phiMc >= 0.43 kNm > 0.363) but drops to 0.16 / 0.13 kNm at L_tw = 2659 / 3122 mm, which would add more failures under the L_out basis.
findings.evidence: analysis/liftcalc/liftcase.py:99 'return L_in, L_out, max(L_in, min(L_out, 1200.0))'; liftcase.py:115 compression_design(L_out, L_in, L_tw). NFT4 (L_in 381, L_out 1561): phiNc = 29.76 kN at L_tw 381, 17.64 at 1200, 12.71 at 1561 (caps.py). post.py [A]: repo 0 over (max 0.910); L_tw = L_out: 4 over (max 1.610); L_tw = L_in: 0 over (max 0.683). minor_ltb.py: lips-in-compression Mo = 0.657 kNm at (3122, 1200) but 0.142 kNm at (3122, 3122). as4600.moment_minor_nominal (as4600.py:255) has no length input.
findings.fix: State and justify the twist restraint. Either (a) accept torsional restraint at each dimple joint that has screws through both flanges (truss web panel points, noggings). Show this with a stiffness check; the stiffness model already assumes out-of-plane continuity there (rz = 1). Then set L_tw = joint spacing, or 0.8 x nogging spacing for studs per the housing-industry note in the research file. Or (b) add steel bridging/blocking to the roof truss chords and studs so the documented L_out works. Code the minor-axis lateral buckling check with the same lengths, and use one twist length for compression and bending (see the note on lb = L_in).

findings.title: Cradle / foot-plate screw check pools 3 stations; the plate-end stations are over
findings.detail: run_connectors.py sums |node force| over the 6 framed nodes within 150 mm of the strap and compares the sum with 24 screws. The 'total' row sums all 14 nodes against 56 screws. But each node is one chord at one station, and only its own 4 screws (2 faces x 2) can carry its force: 4 x 1.77 x 0.9 = 6.37 kN. In the repo's own model the stiff plate is joined to the chord at rigid shared nodes, so it acts as a doubler. Large forces along the chord therefore enter at the plate-end stations, which are outside the ±150 mm local zone. Per station, 6 of 22 plates are over: VFOOT_N2a 9.22 kN (1.45), VFOOT_N3b 9.20 (1.44), VFOOT_N1a 7.36 (1.16), VFOOT_N4b 7.05 (1.11), STIR_N4 6.82 (1.07), STIR_N1 6.78 (1.06). Foot plates are modelled with the 2.5 mm cradle properties, but connectors.md specifies 2.0 mm. Rerun with 0.8 x stiffness: still 1.33. As modelled, the end stations sit exactly at the plate edges, so the screws there have no end distance in the plate. The research file's verify section says groups of more than 5 screws are outside the tested range: check block tear-out, and prove the group by test or use bolts. Commit 0ffaff8 now labels the temporary foot plates 'bolted', but run_connectors.py still checks them as screwed.
findings.evidence: analysis/run_connectors.py:80-96 (loc/tot sums; n_local = 3*2*2*2, n_total = 7*2*2*2); run_lift.py:43,56-62,94 (stirrup props reused for VFOOT, chord attachments at the plate ends). plate_nodes_out.txt, VFOOT_N2a in R7b: plate-end station forces (8.28, 0, 4.05) kN = 9.22 kN at x = 3600 bottom chord and 4.77 kN at x = 3000; strap station only 0.93 kN; strap 9.16 kN. Repo's connectors.md shows util 0.17 / 0.37 / 0.51 / 0.47 for these rows. foot_2mm_out.txt: 1.33 at 2.0 mm stiffness.
findings.fix: Check each station's screws against that station's node force, and give the end screws an end distance in the plate. Then either model the plate-to-chord screws as slip springs, or add screws at the end stations (e.g. 3 per face per chord), extend or taper the plate ends, or through-bolt. If the temporary foot plates are bolted, check M12 bearing on the 0.95 mm chord plies at 5.21 kN per bolt per ply (J3.3.2 at 412.5 MPa). Make H4 a capacity test of the large screw groups, not only a proof load, or carry the load in bolts as the research file recommends.

findings.title: Stud bases pass only with bearing credit; no end-gap limit and no web crippling check
findings.detail: check_joints sets the axial demand to zero for a wall stud in compression standing square on a plate, so the 2 screws there carry shear only. Without that credit, 6 south-wall stud-base joints (2 screws, 3.54 kN) are over: W7 x=4202 6.45 kN (1.82), W9 x=10802 5.28 kN (1.49), W9 x=7802 1.21, W8 x=4802 1.14, W6 x=602 1.11, W7 x=1202 1.04. Framer studs are swaged and dimpled into the track. With any end gap, the screws carry the load until the gap closes; the design basis states no gap tolerance and no inspection. The bearing path itself is never checked: no web crippling (AS/NZS 4600 3.3.6) or crippling + bending (3.3.7) of the track and floor-rim chord under studs, and none under the cradle base. My estimate uses the AISI G5 IOF form, with the two 38 mm C flanges of the rim chord acting as webs and N = 38 mm. It gives phiPw about 16.8 kN, so util about 0.38 at 6.45 kN: crippling is unlikely to govern, but the check is missing.
findings.evidence: analysis/liftcalc/liftcase.py:180-182 (square = ... ; Nj = 0.0 if bearing_ok and N < 0 and square). bearing_off_out.txt: 6 of 2210 joints over 1.0 with bearing_ok=False (max 1.82). Wall panels W5-W11 keep the default 2 screws per joint (only W1-W4 and NFT2 are raised, revC_design.json:183-189). No web-crippling function exists anywhere (grep 'crippl' finds none).
findings.fix: Add a hold point limiting the stud end gap (checked before the lift) for the studs whose joints rely on bearing, or give those stud bases enough screws for the full compression (6.45 kN needs at least 6 at 1.77 x 0.9). Add a web crippling + bending check (AS/NZS 4600 3.3.6 / 3.3.7) at bearing points: stud or post on track over the rim chord, and the cradle base under the bottom chord.

findings.title: Screw end distance and end rupture not checked; Framer brace-end screws are below the code minimum
findings.detail: No check limits screw shear by end distance: as4600.screw_tearout_design exists but is never called, and the design basis gives no minimum end distance. framed.json gives each dimple's position from the member end. Wall DIAGONAL BRACE ends are at 2.8-4.2 mm (66 joint ends below 1.5d = 7.3 mm, the AS/NZS / AISI minimum). Truss webs are at 9.1-11 mm: 804 joint ends below 2d = 9.7 mm, and 1608 below 3 df = 14.6 mm, which the research basis requires along with the AISI end-rupture form at phi 0.50. Braces are in tension in the lift (up to 1.91 kN factored). With the repo's own (unused) form 0.60 t e fu, brace W7 goes from repo util 0.54 to 1.43 and W9 from 0.40 to 1.06. With AISI J6 (e_net = e - d/2, phi 0.5), 20 brace-end joints exceed 1.0. For truss webs at e = 9.1 mm, J6 gives 1.57 kN per screw (-11 %), so the worst joint goes from 0.83 to about 0.94: no fail, but below the basis rule.
findings.evidence: analysis/liftcalc/as4600.py:351 (screw_tearout_design, unused); framed.json W7-D diagonal brace joints at [4.2, 791.7] of L 799.1; end_dist_out.txt (band counts, 20 joints over with J6, 2 with the AS form, top: W7 brace e 2.9 mm, T 1.91 kN, util 0.54 -> 1.43). Research file recommended_basis: per-screw capacity includes 'the AISI end shear rupture' and 'end distance in the line of force at least 3 df'.
findings.fix: Confirm Framer's dimple-to-end geometry at mitred brace ends. Require at least 1.5d, and preferably 3 df as the research basis asks, in the line of force for every lift-path screw. Add an end-rupture check (lower of AS/NZS 5.4.2.5 and AISI J6 at phi 0.50) to check_joints / check_links / connectors. Relocate or add screws at the diagonal-brace ends. The extra 4- and 6-screw joints must meet 3d spacing and the end distances inside the 38 mm flange overlap; show the screw pattern.

findings.title: Framer operations (lip notches, swages, service and web holes) are not in any capacity
findings.detail: Every member is checked as a plain unperforated C89 (sections.py, as4600.LippedChannel, FSM table for the plain section). framed.json lists: 2396 LIP NOTCH (at every truss-chord web joint: 336 on floor truss top chords, 112-116 per rim/roof-rim chord); 2290 SWAGE (all truss web ends and stud ends); 59 SERVICE HOLE (30 in studs, including W7-AC and W9-AC, the two most compressed studs at 6.45 and 5.28 kN, each with a hole at 295.5 mm); 100 WEB NOTCH (noggings, headers, sills). Lip notches remove the edge stiffener of the compression-chord flange exactly at the panel points. The unstiffened 36 mm flange (k = 0.43) has fcr about 54 MPa, against about 500 MPa when lipped. A crude EWM upper bound at NFT4's notch (lips removed, fn = 160 MPa) gives phiN about 12 kN, vs 17.6 kN for the plain section, with N = 13.2 kN. The swaged web inside the notch restrains the flanges, so the real loss is smaller, but nothing covers it. DESIGN_BASIS does not mention these operations.
findings.evidence: model/engineered/framed.json member 'ops' counts: LIP NOTCH 2396, SWAGE 2290, WEB NOTCH 100, SERVICE HOLE 59 (STUD 30, KING STUD 10, CRIPPLE 8, DIAGONAL BRACE 11). Studs with service holes include W7-AC (x 4202) and W9-AC (x 10802).
findings.fix: Obtain the Framer / roll-former test basis for notched-chord / swaged-web joints and for studs with service holes and adopt it. Otherwise check the notched and holed sections (FSM of the notched/holed section, AS/NZS 4600:2018 Section 7 or AISI members with holes), or forbid service holes in lift-critical members, and say so in DESIGN_BASIS.

findings.title: Member shear and combined bending + shear are not checked
findings.detail: LippedChannel.shear_design is never called, and there is no AS/NZS 4600 3.3.4 / 3.3.5 check. My check over the design envelope: in-plane shear (carried by the two flanges, phiV 17.8 kN) peaks at util 0.35 (NFT2 rim bottom chord 6.27 kN). (M/phiM)^2 + (V/phiV)^2 peaks at 0.43 (W4 bottom track). Web (out-of-plane) shear capacity is 8.56 kN. Not governing now, but required.
findings.evidence: as4600.py:283-294 (unused); post_out.txt section [B].
findings.fix: Add shear about both axes and the bending + shear interaction to check_members.

findings.title: Minor-axis 0.363 kNm: basis needs stating; lips-in-compression distortional check not coded
findings.detail: 0.363 kNm is DSM local buckling (web in compression) with phi_b 0.90. Minor-axis bending of a lipped C is not a pre-qualified DSM beam case, and the DSM rules use phi 0.80 for sections outside the pre-qualified limits, which gives 0.323 kNm. The EWM route (phi 0.90; my estimate: web effective width 41 of 87 mm, first yield at the lips) gives about 0.46 kNm, so 0.363 is covered. But the docstring's 'both routes evaluated, lower governs' is not what the code does: for minor-axis bending, EWM is only a fallback. The FSM table gives f_dist = 417 MPa for lips in compression and its own note says a distortional check is needed. The code ignores it (phiMd = 0.387 kNm); it does not govern only because min(web, lips) is taken.
findings.evidence: as4600.py:255-280; c89_buckling.json bend_minor_lips_comp f_dist 417.07 with usage note; caps.py / caps2.py: DSM 0.4036 kNm nominal, phi 0.9 = 0.3632, phi 0.8 = 0.3229, EWM about 0.516 nominal (0.465 with phi), distortional (lips) 0.4297 nominal.
findings.fix: State EWM (or DSM at phi 0.80) as the basis for minor-axis bending, and add the distortional check for lips in compression.

findings.title: Material strengths for added parts and members do not follow the 'more conservative of AS/NZS and AISI' policy
findings.detail: connectors.py uses G450 at fy 450 / fu 480 for straps, cradles, foot plates and the head. The research file (AISI A3.1.2, 3-10 % elongation, G450 at 9 %) says use 0.9 fy and 0.9 fu (405 / 432 MPa), and AUDIT.md says the more conservative value was taken. Members use fy 450, while the frame steel is treated as low-ductility G550 for connections (412.5). Under that same AISI rule, member fy would be at most about 412.5-414 MPa: phiNc at 600 mm -4.1 %, phiMy -5.5 %. All connector rows still pass at fu 432 (strap net section 0.44, cradle base 0.65), so nothing fails, but the basis is inconsistent. G450 in 2.0-3.0 mm plate needs confirming as an available AS 1397 product.
findings.evidence: analysis/liftcalc/connectors.py:15; research 'Masses and material data' item 29 and recommended_basis[1]; AUDIT.md 'taking the more conservative value'; caps2.py fy 412.5 sensitivity.
findings.fix: Use 0.9 fu / 0.9 fy for the G450 parts in connector checks (or confirm AS/NZS 4600 permits full values and say so), state why member fy 450 is acceptable (AS/NZS 4600 G550 at t >= 0.9 mm), and confirm the plate grades.

findings.title: Bolt tear-out and lifting-head bearing logic
findings.detail: The strap tear-out row uses e = 40 mm (centre-to-centre pitch) for the inner bolt. The clear distance to the adjacent hole is 33 mm, and AISI J6 uses e_net = 26 mm on two planes. Total capacity drops from 30.24 to about 27.3 kN; util 0.22 -> 0.25. The head row adds the M20 pin bearing capacities of the 3 mm cheeks and the 1.5 mm straps as if they shared one force. Each ply should be checked with its own force: hanger strap 6.7 kN on 1.5 mm vs 16.9 kN; V-strap 4.6 kN on 1.2 mm vs 13.1 kN. If the straps hang on the M20 pin, the strap net section at the 22 mm hole (13.1 kN) and the strap tear-out at the pin are unchecked, and the hanger label ('2 x M12 bolts each end') contradicts the head row. Margins are large.
findings.evidence: analysis/run_connectors.py:56 and 112-113; revC_design.json hanger label.
findings.fix: Use the clear distance (or J6 e_net) for inner bolts, check each ply on the pin with its own force, and settle the head detail (pin or 2 x M12) and check the strap end there.

findings.title: Sideways allowance is 10.5 % for the head box but 5 % for the frame and the head-to-roof-rim bolts
findings.detail: The head box and pin rows use 10.5 % of the sling force (6 degree drop tolerance). Load cases L1-L4, and the bolts into the 0.95 mm roof-rim chords (F_scr from the GUIDE forces), use sideways_fraction 0.05. At 10.5 % the bolt demand roughly doubles (3.2 -> about 6.7 kN vs 20.8 kN), and the roof-rim chord moments rise.
findings.evidence: analysis/run_connectors.py:109,117; analysis/configs/revC_design.json:87.
findings.fix: Use one allowance throughout: either 5 % with a rigging limit of about 3 degrees, or 10.5 % in L1-L4 and the bolt check.

findings.title: The capacity module has no unit tests (the cited test file does not exist)
findings.detail: The as4600.py header says the formulas are checked in analysis/tests/test_as4600.py. The tests folder holds only test_beam2d, test_buckling_table, test_fea3d and test_sections, so AUDIT.md's '37 pass' does not cover any capacity function.
findings.evidence: as4600.py:4; ls analysis/tests.
findings.fix: Add tests with these hand values: phiNc(L = 600) = 29.23 kN, phiMy(minor) = 0.3632 kNm, phiMx(lb <= 600) = 1.405 kNm, one screw = 1.770 kN (tilting 3.540 kN nominal), J3.3.2 M12 on 1.5 mm = 10.13 kN and on 0.95 mm at 412.5 MPa = 5.21 kN, M12 shear 30.24 kN.

findings.title: Twist length in major-axis lateral buckling differs from the compression check
findings.detail: moment_major_design(lb = L_in) uses L_in for both lateral movement and twist, while compression uses the capped L_tw. No effect now (Mout <= 0.009 kNm in the governing members), but it should follow whatever twist rule the first finding settles on.
findings.evidence: analysis/liftcalc/liftcase.py:118 vs 99.
findings.fix: Use one twist length in both checks.

findings.title: Joint check ignores member end moments (checked: negligible)
findings.detail: Members are continuous out of plane at their ends (rz = 1), so end moments pass through the screws on the two faces as a couple. check_joints uses forces only. Largest end Mz at a joint is 0.021 kNm; adding 2Mz/88 to the group demand moves the maximum joint util from 0.834 to 0.835.
findings.evidence: post_out.txt section [C].
findings.fix: State the assumption in the basis.

findings.title: Small items in the check code
findings.detail: (a) The log line 'links over 1.0 in shear: 2' is misleading: those 2 links are over in pull-out (shear util 0.25) and are covered by tie T2. (b) Member tension uses An = Ag and kt = 1, i.e. no screw-hole loss and no shear-lag factor for a C connected through its flanges; the margin is large. (c) The cl 2.4.2 limit uses S/3 instead of 0.328 S. (d) G = 80000 MPa in as4600.py vs E/2.6 in the FSM table. (e) The hanger strap pair force is split T/2 per face; no imbalance is allowed for.
findings.fix: Relabel the log line; optionally add the net section and kt; no other change needed.

verified: Section properties of C89x38x9x0.95 (sharp corners): A 170.24 mm2, Ix 216,189 mm4, Iy 33,146 mm4, xc 11.19 mm, x0 28.19 mm, r01 47.53 mm. These match the closed form and my hand calculation; j = 49.8 mm (my calculation).

Compression at lex = ley = lez = 600 mm: foc 721.2 MPa (flexural-torsional governs; foy 1067.6), fn 346.6 MPa, Nce 59.0 kN, Nol 19.74 kN, DSM local Ncl 34.39 kN, phiNc = 29.23 kN; distortional phiNcd = 33.97 kN. Hand calculation = code.

Minor-axis moment 0.363 kNm: My = 0.566 kNm (first yield at the lips, Zy_lip 1258 mm3), Mcrl = Zy_web x 118.16 MPa = 0.336 kNm, lambda 1.298, Mnl = 0.4036 kNm, x 0.90 = 0.3632 kNm. The exact FSM resultant (0.350 kNm) gives 0.3685, so the code is 1.4 % conservative.
Major-axis moment: phiMx = 1.405 kNm for lb <= 600 (distortional governs, Md = 1.561 kNm nominal); EWM Ms 1.725 and DSM local 1.951 kNm nominal.
DSM pre-qualification limits are met for compression and major-axis bending (h/t 93.7, b/t 40, D/t 9.5, h/b 2.34, D/b 0.24, fy <= 593 MPa), so phi 0.85 / 0.90 is valid there.

Axes in check_members are correct: Min = local My (end-force index 4/10, bending in the panel plane = minor axis) is paired with phiMy; Mout = local Mz (index 5/11, out of plane = major axis) with phiMx; lex = L_out and ley = L_in; Nex uses Ix and L_out, Ney uses Iy and L_in; N tension-positive from index 6. Panel normals are horizontal for every panel, so this holds for walls, trusses and rims.

Combined actions: the 3.5.1 form (N/phiNc <= 0.15 linear rule, amplification 1 - N/Ne, Cm = 1.0, second equation with phiNs = 0.85 Ae(fy) fy, which is within 0.5 % of DSM Nl(Ny)) and the 3.5.2 tension + bending form are right, and conservative in using member capacities in the '+N' equation.

Effective width code (2.2.1, 2.3.1, 2.4.2: Ia, n, RI, k for D/b <= 0.25; web under stress gradient k = 24, b1 = be/4, b2 = be/2; neutral-axis shift) and the DSM local / distortional equations for compression and bending match the published forms.

Flexural-torsional buckling formula, beta = 1 - (x0/r01)^2, and foc = min(foy, foxz) with x as the axis of symmetry are correct; the major-axis lateral buckling Mo = Cb A r01 sqrt(foy foz) and its three lambda branches are correct.

Screw shear, AS/NZS 4600 5.4.2.4: tilting 4.2 sqrt(t2^3 d) fu2 = 3.540 kN nominal at 0.95/0.95 mm and 412.5 MPa; bearing factor C 2.7/3.3-0.1d/t/2.0; t2/t1 <= 1, >= 2.5 and interpolation branches correct; phi 0.5 gives 1.770 kN; fracture cap 0.5 x 5.7 = 2.85 kN; the rule that the screw strength is at least 1.25 Vb holds for the tilting case (4.43 <= 5.7 kN). The cradle and foot plates are rightly taken with the thick plate under the screw head (tilting, conservative).
Pull-out 0.5 x 0.85 t d fu (0.81 kN per screw) and pull-over forms are correct; pull-out is used only to flag links that need positive ties.

Bolts: deformation-limited bearing (0.183 t + 1.53) d t fu at phi 0.65 (AISI J3.3.2, SI form) gives M12 on 1.5 mm = 10.13 kN, on 2.5 mm = 18.60 kN, on 0.95 mm at 412.5 MPa = 5.21 kN, M20 on 3 mm = 38.92 kN. Bolt shear 0.8 x 0.62 x 800 x core area: M12 30.24 kN, M20 double shear 178.56 kN (800 MPa < 830, conservative). Strap gross 0.90 Ag fy and net 0.65 An fu (2 bolts in line) = 16.85 kN. Tear-out 0.60 t e fu with phi 0.60 because fu/fy < 1.08 for G450.

Using fu = 412.5 MPa for the 0.95 mm frame steel in connections is conservative against AS/NZS 4600 (G550 at t >= 0.9 mm at 550 MPa; G450 at 480 MPa). The 10 % group reduction for 3 or more screws is applied consistently to joints, links and connectors, and is conservative against AS/NZS 4600 and AISI, which have none.
Web shear capacity 8.56 kN (d1/t 91.7 > 1.415 sqrt(E kv/fy); same as AISI G2.1 Vcr with phi 0.9).

Reproduction: my run of the 11 design cases gives max member util 0.910 (NFT4 top chord) and max joint util 0.834 (NFT1 rim web), matching results/revC_design.log; commit 0ffaff8 changed only labels in run_lift.py.

lens: Independent re-computation: (a) weight and CoG, (b) equalised sling shares, (c) lifting-head equilibrium and strap split, (d) north floor rim as a beam/frame on its pick-ups, (e) one floor truss in service, (f) connector-table numbers
summary:
Most of the headline numbers re-derive correctly with my own code. The weight (63.743 kN), the CoG (my value 5976.8 / 1388.6 / 1206.9 mm against the model's 5977.6 / 1388.3 / 1196.8), the south/north shares (0.5814/0.4186, matching R4 within 0.03 %), the head equilibrium (residual below 0.001 N) and almost every connector capacity all agree. The floor-truss end web force of 8.4 kN is also right: my own 2D frame on the real geometry gives 7.95-8.32 kN.

The most important finding is new and comes out of check (c). At each lift point the hanger and the V-straps meet on one pin, are bolted in 14 mm holes, and their share of the load is set by how they are fitted, not by statics. summary:
I reproduced the Rev C results exactly in memory, without editing any repo file: max member 0.91 (NFT4 top chord), max joint 0.83, 117 ties, and the same added-part forces. I then ran about 30 targeted variants of the design cases.

**What holds up.** The global idealisation is robust. Changing any of these moves the max member and max joint utilisations by 0.03 or less, apart from the expected drop in joint demand when joints are made stiffer in plane:
- in-plane joint fixity (0, 0.5, 1)
- out-of-plane fixity (rigid, or r = 0.1)
- link stiffness (x0.2, x5, or the same stiffness for every link whatever its length)
- the 100 mm cradle stations
- the stiffness of the truss-end ties
- plane-brace stiffness (half and quarter)
- the foot-plate thickness

The supports are statically determinate: in every forces-mode case the 3 vertical holds and 3 anti-drift restraints react 0.000 kN. Moments that the checks ignore are negligible: out-of-plane end moments at joints are at most 0.3 N·m, and link moments at most 21 N·m (a 0.36 kN screw couple). I grouped all 2407 unconnected near pairs: none is a missing structural connection, and I found no spurious links.

**What does not hold up.** The result depends on three idealisations of how load is shared inside each lift point. None of them is guaranteed by the stated details, and each can push utilisation past 1.0:
1. **Hanger / V-strap split.** It is statically indeterminate. The model takes it from elastic, no-slip stiffness of thin straps fixed with M12 bolts in 14 mm holes. Plausible fit-up takes the frame from 0.91 to 1.12–3.10 (critical).
2. **Head slots.** The head bracket's vertical slots are assumed frictionless. If they bind, the roof rim bottom chord reaches 1.45 and the T2 ties 1.97 (major).
3. **Cradle and foot plates.** They are modelled as rigid panels fused to the rim chords. Single screw stations reach 1.45, which the averaged connector check does not see. With point stirrups the frame is at 1.00 / 1.01 (major).

There are also smaller gaps:
- **Mass distribution.** The weighing hold point checks total mass and plan centre of gravity, not distribution. With the margin on the floor, the end-return wall bottom tracks reach 0.97.
- **Stud bearing.** Six stud joints rely on studs bearing on the track; if a stud is not seated the joint reaches 1.82.
- **Lateral restraint.** The rim chords are assumed fully restrained at every truss link, but the frame's restraint stiffness is only about equal to the AISC demand.
- **Documentation.** The link-stiffness statement and the truss count in DESIGN_BASIS.md are wrong.

findings.title: Load split between the vertical hanger and the V-straps at each lift point is indeterminate and governed by unmodelled bolt slip / fit-up
findings.detail: At each head the hanger pair (A=150) and the V-strap pair(s) (A=120) share the drop force according to their elastic axial stiffness, with the frame deflection between the V-strap feet and the cradle (run_lift.py:34-36, 81-93; revC_design.json hanger/v_strap). The strap elongation at the design force is tiny: about 0.4 mm per V-strap at rated load (R4: VSTR_S1a 2.65 kN / 6.8 kN/mm) and about 1.3 mm at the factored level. Every strap end is 2 x M12 in 14 mm holes (run_connectors.py:53 and 60 use hole=14.0). That is 2 mm clearance per hole, and up to about 4 mm per bolted joint, two joints per strap. No tensioner, fitted bolt, slip-critical joint or fit-up procedure is specified (IFC definitions 'HS ... 2 x M12 each end', 'VS ... 2 x M12 each end'). I applied a lack of fit as an equivalent pre-strain load, at the factored level (delta/2.433 in the rated solve), with the tension-only iteration. findings.title: Cradle and foot plates modelled as rigid truss panels fused to the rim chords: single-station screw forces exceed capacity and are not checked

This shear-lag model sends large forces into the panel end stations. The connector check (run_connectors.py:65-96) sums node-force magnitudes over the whole plate and compares them with 24 or 56 screws, so peak stations are never checked. The panel stiffness is worth part of the frame margin. The temporary foot plates FP-T, where the largest station forces occur, are 'bolted' (IFC definition), so bolt slip in clearance holes makes the rigid-panel assumption even less realistic. The foot plates are also modelled with the 2.5 mm cradle properties, while the connector sheet and IFC specify 2.0 mm (D17 showed no effect on the frame).

lens: Load cases, factors and rigging (cascade behaviour, tilt and CoG envelope, sideways, skew, lift-off, set-down, temporary straps, rigid frame, rigging hardware)
summary:
I added the missing rig cases in scratch copies and ran them on the repo's own model and checks (C0 reproduces R4 exactly: 0.907 / 0.627). R4 does model a real 1-2-4-8 pinned-beam cascade with every transverse beam picked off-centre at the CoG: my explicit cascade case C1 gives the same results.

The main gap is that every design case puts either vertical loads or self-cancelling sideways sets on the lifting heads. No case puts a net horizontal load on the module. That load comes from the 2-degree hang angle the basis allows, from a CoG offset under a determinate rig, from wind, from slewing and from tag lines. A 2-degree roll alone overloads the end-wall stud-base joints: utilisation 1.11 to 1.16 (3.9 to 4.1 kN on 2 screws, capacity 3.54 kN). It also overloads one wall-to-floor tie: 3.64 to 3.77 kN on a T2 tie rated 3.54 kN. The joint utilisation rises by about 0.58 per degree and crosses 1.0 at about 1.7 degrees. A 2-degree pitch takes the governing member (NFT4 top chord) to 1.00 in the model as built. This is partly a modelling artefact: it drops to 0.66 when the mid-span bridging the design calls for is modelled as a member.

The first lift is made before the CoG is known. Hold points H1 and H5 cannot give the CoG with a determinate rig, because the drop loads are fixed by the rig geometry and the CoG error shows only as tilt. At the DNV minimum CoG envelope that lift reaches joint utilisations of 1.33 to 1.45.

Landing and storage supports are not specified anywhere:
* Corner-only supports fail by about 5x at a static factor.
* On the 8 cradle positions alone, one support 5 mm low gives 1.82.
* Continuous bearers with a 10 mm low zone 6 m long fail.
* Piers at 1.8 m or closer, or continuous level bearers, pass.

Lift-off with one end still seated is harmless.

The temporary north V-straps are needed for the lift but appear nowhere in the design basis or hold points. Without them the N rim reaches 1.21 in the R7b skew case, 1.05 under a 2-degree tilt and 1.33 under the first-lift tilt.

The +/-10 % skew patterns are never combined with tilt. Combining R7d with a 2-degree roll gives 1.43 to 1.50, even after strengthening the end walls. R7c ('one end high') is mislabelled: the force balancing removes its end-to-end moment.

The factor stack (2.433) is at or above DNV, and the 1.12 t static drop is correct. 2 t round slings and 3.2 / 3.25 t shackles have ample WLL. The head-pin, shackle and sling interface is ambiguous, and read literally it breaks the sling and lug rules in the research. The cascade beams themselves have no design, certification or rating hold point.

Transport is out of scope but will probably govern wall racking: the 0.5 g lateral case is roughly 5 to 10 times the 2-degree roll effect.

findings.title: No design case puts a net horizontal load on the module; the stated 2-degree hang angle overloads end-wall stud-base joints and a wall-to-floor tie
findings.detail:
The basis allows a hang angle of at most 2 degrees. Under a determinate cascade, a CoG mismatch e makes the module hang tilted by atan(e/h), with h = 1953 mm from the heads down to the CoG. The drop forces stay as the rig sets them. In the module frame each drop then pulls sideways at its head by F sin(theta), and the gravity component acts on every mass node in the opposite direction.

No design case represents this. R1-R7 are vertical only, and L1-L4 apply self-cancelling squeeze/spread sets at the heads (each sums to zero), so neither tests the racking path. The CoG factor 1.05 only scales the whole load uniformly, and DNV allows a factor only where the effect varies linearly with the offset.

I modelled tilt self-consistently: rig shares from the cascade with the pick point offset by e, gravity and drops resolved in the module frame. All support reactions came out exactly zero.

Roll (across the module): the head boxes take the horizontal head force into the roof plane. The floor's sideways inertia has to rack up through the two end walls only (no lining credit). The end-wall stud-base joints have 2 screws, and the wall-bottom-track ties are T2 straps.

Pitch: with the model as built, NFT4 top chord reaches 1.004. This is a modelling artefact: the 120 kg joinery lump sits as a point load at one mid-span node, and the bridging is only a buckling length, not a member. With the bridging modelled as a C89 member, the pitch effect is benign (0.66).

Wind at the H6 limit adds about 0.5-0.75 degrees of equivalent roll (lightest unit). Slewing and tag lines add more.

findings.title: H1 and H5 cannot give the CoG with a determinate cascade, so the first lift is made with an unverified CoG
findings.detail:
H1 says to weigh at the 8 lift points and let the measured CoG set the pick points. With a determinate pinned-beam cascade, each drop load equals the hook load times a ratio fixed by the rig geometry, whatever the mass distribution. By statics x_g = p - h tan(theta): the shackles only return p (already known from the rig), so the CoG has to come from the measured hang angle (and the CoG height).

H5 ('stop if any drop is more than 15 % from its design share') therefore only detects a rig malfunction, such as a seized pin, a fouled sling or a beam bearing on the roof. It cannot detect a CoG error or tilt.

The first (weighing) lift is made with picks set to the computed CoG. The 6.5 t rating hides up to 1.7 t of unknown mass, so the CoG uncertainty can exceed DNV's minimum envelope (+/-0.30 m along, +/-0.083 m across).

docs/DESIGN_BASIS.md:20 (share fixed by statics), :62-63 (H1), :69 (H5).

* NFT4 top chord 1.32

Find mass and CoG before setting the picks by one of two methods:
* weigh on calibrated load cells at 3-4 ground support points; or
* make a controlled 'just clear' first lift, measure pitch and roll with an inclinometer, use e = h tan(theta) with h of about 1.95 m, lower and re-set.

Add a hang-angle stop criterion to H5 (the limit from the critical finding). Keep the 15 % drop-load rule as a rig-malfunction check. State the pick-point adjustment resolution: about 34 mm per degree, so +/-25 mm or finer.

findings.title: Landing and storage supports are not specified; corner-only or uneven supports overload the frame several times over

The lift basis assumes in-service continuous bearers but says nothing about landing. I ran the support cases with one-way supports: a bearer can only push, and a low bearer touches only if the module deflects into it.

findings.title: The +/-10 % skew patterns are never combined with tilt or sideways loads; R7d plus a 2-degree roll fails even after strengthening the end walls
findings.detail:
DNV-OS-H205 combines the skew factor with the weight, CoG and dynamic factors. It does not treat skew as a separate case. The design runs R7a-d with no sideways or tilt load, and runs L1-L4 with no skew.

A pinned determinate cascade justifies skew 1.0 physically: pin friction moves the split by under 0.5 %. So either the +/-10 % patterns are a robustness margin and should be stated as such, or they are a design allowance and must be combined with the tilt envelope.

Combined, the end floor trusses (NFT3 / NFT23) web joints, the end-wall bottom tracks and the T2 ties fail.

Decide and state the basis.
* Option 1: skew 1.0 (pinned determinate beams, pick holes to +/-5 mm), keeping R7a-d as robustness checks. Then the tilt envelope from the critical finding governs.
* Option 2: keep the 10 % allowance and add combined skew + tilt + sideways cases, then strengthen the end floor truss web joints (6 screws at the interior web joints of NFT3 / NFT23) and the end-wall bottom tracks and ties.

findings.title: Rigging interface and rig equipment not defined: shackle-to-head arrangement unclear; cascade beams have no design, certification or rating hold point
findings.detail:
The WLL numbers check out: 1.12 t static drop against a 2 t round sling (56 %) and a 3.2 / 3.25 t bow shackle (35 %). The arrangement 'bow shackles over the sleeved M20 head pin' is ambiguous, and both readings break the research's own rules:
* If the bow sits on the head pin, the round sling ends up on the 19 mm shackle pin inside a 27 mm jaw. A 2 t round sling body is 37-48 mm wide, and the research says the sling goes in the bow; DNV says avoid pinching.
* If the shackle pin passes through the head, the 3 mm cheeks plus 1.5 mm straps are not a lug of at least 0.75 x 27 = 20.3 mm.

It is also not stated whether the sleeve is rounded, or whether the round sling bears on 3 mm cheek edges.

The cascade is part of the design, but its seven beams are lifting equipment with no AS 4991 design, proof test, rating, mass or hook-load statement. The transverse beams need an off-centre pick at about 1343 mm from the S drop, with adjustment resolution of about +/-25 mm to hold roll under about 1 degree. The beam spans must match 3211 mm (across), 3600 mm (mid beams) and 6600 mm (top beam) closely enough to keep the drops within 2 degrees.
findings.evidence:
analysis/run_connectors.py:152-155 (static = head_max x 1.03 x 1.05 = 10.128 x 1.0815 = 10.95 kN = 1.12 t; recommendation text). results/revC_design/connectors.md: head pin checks only.

Research:
* verify[1] unsafe[8]: 3.2 t bow shackle, sling in the bow, lug at least 20.3 mm thick, hole no more than 20.1 mm
* items 'round_sling_size_and_shackle_fit' and 'shackle_bow_grade_s_3p2t': pin 19, jaw 27, bow 43 mm
* verify[1] unsafe[3] (planning hook load about 8.7 t), unsafe[5] (beam span to lug centres), missing[20] (AS 4991 proof multiple)
findings.fix:
Draw the head-pin, shackle and sling interface. For example, sling eye directly on a free-turning sleeve of adequate diameter inside the head box, with rounded edges and a cut guard, and the shackle at the beam end with the sling in the bow. Alternatively, a proper lug (20.3 mm or more with bosses) for the shackle pin.

Add a hold point for the cascade: designed and certified as lifting equipment (AS 4991), proof tested, rated, beam masses known, pick-hole pitch stated. State the planning hook load (module x 1.10 until weighed, plus rig and block) on the lift plan.

findings.title: R7c 'one end high' is not modelled as labelled; the real pitch case under a cascade is missing
findings.detail:
balance_forces makes the smallest vertical correction that restores equilibrium. That correction removes the whole end-to-end moment of the R7c step pattern, leaving a residual inner/outer pattern of (-0.19, +0.65, -0.65, +0.19) x 10 % of W/8 per line.

Under a determinate cascade, a top-beam split error does not redistribute vertically. The module pitches instead, adding horizontal components (see the T2_P cases). R7a, R7b and R7d sum to zero and are unaffected.
findings.evidence:
analysis/run_lift.py:158 (forces always rebalanced), :208 (R7c pattern).

results/revC_design.log R7c row: S1 9.2, S2 9.8, S3 8.7, S4 9.4 kN. Hand calculation of the residual: 9.15 / 9.82 / 8.68 / 9.35, a match. This is not one end high.

T2_P+/-: NFT4 1.004 in the model as built, 0.66 with bridging.
findings.fix: Rename R7c to what it is, or replace it with pitch cases. In those, the rig shares are fixed for p = x_g +/- e and the module is tilted by atan(e/h), as in the critical finding.

findings.title: Weight factor applied twice, and the weighing tolerance may not support 1.03
findings.detail:
H1 caps the weighed mass x 1.03 at 6,500 kg, and the analysis then applies 1.03 again to 6,500 kg. The effective factor on the weighed mass is 1.061: conservative but unstated.

DNV allows 1.03 only with a documented weighing tolerance better than +/-3 %. Eight 3.25 t load shackles at +/-1 % of full scale give up to +/-260 kg (+/-4.0 %) if their errors run the same way.
findings.evidence: docs/DESIGN_BASIS.md:28 and :62. analysis/configs/revC_design.json:6. Research verify[2] missing[1] (1.03 only if weighed within +/-3 %). Research item 'load_measuring_shackles' (+/-1 % of full scale).
findings.fix: Apply 1.03 once, and say where. Weigh with a calibrated hook load cell or ground load cells, each better than +/-1 % of reading, and record the tolerance. Use 1.10 on the estimate until weighed; it is covered by the 1.35 rating margin.

findings.title: Comparison with the DNV consequence factor is not like for like
findings.detail:
The basis compares 2.433 with DNV's 1.3 x 1.3 x 1.1 = 1.86. DNV's own minimum DAF is 1.10 onshore. If the Australian DAF of 1.5 is kept, adding DNV's 1.3 consequence factor for lift points and their attachments gives 1.03 x 1.05 x 1.5 x 1.69 = 2.74, which is 12.7 % above 2.433.

The current lift-point utilisations still pass when scaled: up to 0.59 in connectors.md becomes 0.67, and rim web joints at the cradles go from 0.83 to 0.94. In a determinate cascade every part of the lift path is a single critical element (R5 shows total loss).
findings.evidence: docs/DESIGN_BASIS.md:31-34. Research verify[1] missing[6] (1.3 x 1.3 at lift points, 1.3 x 1.15 for supporting members). results/revC_design/connectors.md (largest lift-point utilisation 0.59).
findings.fix: State the basis: DNV in full (DAF 1.10, design total 2.01, leaving 21 % reserve), or Australian DAF 1.5 with a consequence factor of 1.13 on lift points and attachments. List which parts count as lift-point attachments.

findings.title: Sideways magnitudes are inconsistent (5 % of W/8 in the frame cases, 10.5 % at the head)
findings.detail:
L1-L4 apply 0.05 x W/8 = 0.40 kN at every head. That is only 4.3 % of a south drop force and less than the stated rig limits (2 deg drop + 2 deg hang, about 7 %). run_connectors uses 10.5 % (6 deg drop) at the head.

I ran self-cancelling cases at 7 % and 10.5 % of each drop's own force. Neither changes the result, so this is a consistency fix only.
findings.evidence: analysis/run_lift.py:220. analysis/configs/revC_design.json:87. analysis/run_connectors.py:109. Scratch S070_* / S105_*: member 0.91, joints up to 0.67.
findings.fix: Use one stated sideways fraction (10.5 %, or 7 % if the 2-degree drop limit goes on the drawing) applied to each drop's own force. Keep the net-horizontal tilt cases separate (critical finding).

findings.title: Rigid-frame fallback ('measured leg loads within +/-10 %') is untested
findings.detail:
The exclusion of a rigid frame is sound and conservative. R6 shows joints up to 2.09 for a 10 mm sling error with k = 2000 N/mm (about a 2 m wire-rope sling). Round slings are softer but have larger length tolerances, so the conclusion holds.

The fallback sentence, however, has not been checked. R7a-d are four global patterns, while a rigid frame produces local single-leg patterns (the R6 type).
findings.evidence: docs/DESIGN_BASIS.md:22-23. results/revC_design.log R6_* (members up to 1.60, joints up to 2.09, links up to 3.47).
findings.fix: Delete the conditional sentence, or check single-leg +/-10 % patterns (R6 scaled) before allowing it.

findings.title: Tie schedule is incomplete for tilt cases
findings.detail: Under a 2-degree roll, 10-12 link positions that are not in the 117-link tie schedule exceed the 10 %-of-pull-out tension threshold. At the first-lift envelope it is 15-17. Their tensions are small (no more than 0.57-0.72 kN), but the design rule is that no screw is relied on in pull-out. One existing T2 tie also exceeds capacity: 3.64 kN on 3.54 kN.
findings.evidence:
Script tie_schedule.py:
* T2_Q+: 12 new ties (7 floor truss chord-end, 4 wall seam, 1 bottom track)
* F1_Q+: 17 new ties
* ties above 3.54 kN: 'wall bottom track on floor rim' 3.64 (T2_Q+), 4.17 / 4.41 (F1_Q+)
findings.fix: Regenerate the tie schedule from an envelope that includes the tilt cases.

findings.title: Minimum-weight, wind and tag-line horizontal loads are not considered
findings.detail: For the lightest unit (4.8 t) at the H6 gust limit (3.7 m/s, Cd 2.0, 38.4 m2, about 0.66 kN at mid-height), the module rolls about 0.74 degrees. This adds directly to the CoG roll. The basis gives no designated tag-line points; DNV asks for 1.3 x the line load.
findings.evidence: Hand calculation: 0.66 kN x 1.8 m = 47.2 kN x 1.953 m x sin(phi), so phi = 0.74 deg. Research verify[2] missing[8] (tag lines), missing[9] (wind on the unit). docs/DESIGN_BASIS.md:70-71.
findings.fix: Include wind (minimum weight) and slew/tag-line accelerations in the tilt envelope. Designate and check tag-line points.

findings.title: The governing member (0.91) is a modelling artefact that is sensitive to lateral load
findings.detail: NFT4 top chord governs at 0.91 because the 120 kg joinery lump is applied at a single mid-span node of one truss, and the mid-span bridging the design calls for exists only as a buckling length. Modelled as a C89 member, the bridging shares the lump and the nominal maximum member utilisation drops to 0.64. The same artefact makes the as-built model show 1.00 under a 2-degree pitch and 1.32 under 8.7 degrees.
findings.evidence: Script diag_nft4.py: C1 Mout 0.0001, T2P+ Mout 0.1268 kNm (factored), N unchanged at -13.1 kN. out_bridging.log: C1 member 0.64.
findings.fix: Model the bridging as members and spread the lumped fit-out masses over their footprint. This is for the mass-model and frame lenses.

findings.title: Transport is out of scope but will likely govern wall racking and support layout
findings.detail: The 2-degree roll is a sideways load of about 3.5 % g at the lift factor 2.433 (8.5 % g design). A Load Restraint Guide lateral case of 0.5 g with a load factor of about 1.5 is roughly 9 times that. Allowing for the different load path, that is roughly 5 to 10 times the end-wall racking demand: about 10 times over for unstrengthened joints without lining credit. Self-weight alone on corner supports fails by about 4-5 times.
findings.evidence: 0.5 x 1.5 / (0.0349 x 2.433) = 8.8. SD_4corners_level_H0: 5.43 at 1.35 x 1.03 x rated, about 3.9 at 1.35 x itemised.
findings.fix: Flag in the basis that transport (support layout, restraint, racking) must be designed separately before the first move.

verified: R4 matches a real 1-2-4-8 pinned-beam cascade with transverse beams picked off-centre at the CoG: an explicit cascade (top beam at x_g, mid beams centre-picked, S share 0.5815) gives identical utilisations (member 0.907, joint 0.627) and drop forces within 0.1 kN of R4 (S1 9.33 / N1 6.71 kN).
Scratch reproduction of R4 matches the log (0.907 / 0.627); PyNite agreement was taken as given.
The tilt cases are fully balanced: support reactions are 0.000 N in pure roll; in the 8.7 / 2.4 degree combination the residual is under 21 N (0.03 % of W).
Factor stack 1.03 x 1.05 x 1.5 x 1.5 = 2.433 is applied uniformly. It is at or above DNV-OS-H205 with the onshore DAF of 1.10: 2.01 at lift points, 1.78 for main supporting members.
DAF 1.5 is conservative against DNV's onshore 1.10 and matches the Australian certificate practice; the H6 conditions match the research.
The H6 wind limit (2.4-3.7 m/s gust for a 9 m/s chart) matches the research correction.
Skew 1.0 for a pinned determinate cascade is physically justified: pin friction is under 0.5 % of the split. Banning doubled slings over hooks or sheaves is consistent with the research (1.1 / 1.2).
The R7a, R7b and R7d patterns already balance, so the force correction leaves them unchanged (only R7c is altered).
Max static drop 1.12 t = 10.128 kN x 1.03 x 1.05 = 10.95 kN. This is 56 % of a 2 t round sling and about 35 % of a 3.2 / 3.25 t shackle, and inside the research's derived 0.98-1.18 t range.
M20 head pin, cheek bearing and tear-out checks in connectors.md agree with run_connectors.py: 24.78 kN = 10.128 x 2.433 combined with 10.5 % sideways.
Excluding the rigid lifting frame is conservative and consistent with the log: R6 gives joints up to 2.09, members 1.58 and links 3.47 for a 10 mm short sling at k = 2000 N/mm.
Self-cancelling sideways cases at 7 % and 10.5 % of each drop's own force do not change the envelope (member 0.91, joints up to 0.67).

Pitch within 2 degrees is benign once the bridging is modelled as a member (member 0.66, joints 0.64). Straps, V-straps, head box and plane bracing stay within the connector checks in all tilt cases (STRAP up to 12.96 kN, V-STRAP up to 11.28 kN, GUIDE V up to 4.57 kN and M up to 0.767 kNm, plane brace up to 1.58 kN).

Lift-off with the x = 12 m end still seated on a 400 mm bearer is benign under a determinate cascade. For a 300 mm CoG error the hook takes 0.948 W and the bearer 3.19 kN; for 68 mm the bearer takes 0.75 kN. Utilisations are unchanged (lift factor 0.91 / 0.66; static 0.52 / 0.38).
Landing on level continuous bearers, on piers at 1.8 m or closer (even with one pier missing), or on all 8 cradle positions when level, passes: static 0.52 / 0.48, lift factor 0.91 / 0.85.
The heads (z = 3150) are 1.95 m above the CoG (z = 1197), so the cascade hangs stably. The 2-degree hang limit corresponds to e = 68 mm.
The working-tree change to run_lift.py during the review only adds labels and 'temporary' flags; the analysis numbers are unchanged.
